## Trial `mariadb-galera-scale-out-ubuntu1__YNDvH8U`

**Verifier decision: Unsuccessful.** The executor never achieved a working three-node Galera cluster, let alone the four-node expansion. The session was consumed almost entirely by repeated apt-get failures — proxy read timeouts, IPv6 connectivity problems to Ubuntu archive mirrors, and stale apt locks — and by the time the run timed out after 2100 seconds, mariadb-server-10.0 and galera-3 package installation was still in progress (or had not yet reached completion) on all four nodes, with the mariadb service confirmed inactive everywhere it was checked. No wsrep cluster status, no Galera configuration files, no data replication, and no client write test were ever observed. The final executor status of 'blocked/timed out' with zero actions_performed accurately reflects the captured evidence.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.000 | 1.000 | 0.000 | 0.550 | 0.950 | 36/15 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Not satisfied:** Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** Initial discovery commands confirm no MariaDB was installed or active on node1-node3 before the executor's work (mysql not found, systemctl inactive). The executor spent the entire session fighting apt-get network/lock issues and never completed package installation on any node — install.log shows package downloads still in progress (mariadb-server-10.0 not yet configured) at the final observed timestamp on node1, and similar or earlier stages on node2-node4. No wsrep/Galera cluster status, no application data, and no completed installation were ever observed. The task run ended in a timeout with zero cluster formation.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-03ccf83a4dcb477e`, `cmd-efb602167a814245`, `cmd-8caa96bbed4b4b99`, `cmd-bb32b99e52a54028`, `cmd-c0ef7527606e4070`
- **req-2 — Not satisfied:** Add node4 as a fourth Galera member carrying existing data and accepting writes
  - **Why:** node4 never had MariaDB/Galera installed successfully; the final observed command on node4 shows the apt-get install still mid-download (galera-3 package still being fetched), with mariadb service inactive. There is no evidence of node4 joining any cluster, receiving SST/data sync, or accepting writes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cdd448014db5452d`, `cmd-c0ef7527606e4070`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.550**. The executor's mutations were largely legitimate troubleshooting attempts to work around persistent apt-get network timeouts (proxy read timeouts, IPv6 connectivity failures to archive.ubuntu.com) rather than unnecessary experimentation unrelated to the task. It appended cluster hostnames to /etc/hosts on node1 (cmd-635afe86167f4ad3 confirms this took effect) — a reasonable prerequisite for cluster formation, left in place and not harmful. It killed stuck apt-get processes and removed apt lock files (cmd-395cf1387cde42b8, cmd-2c6501f4a3e241de) after processes appeared hung — a corrective action to unblock retries, low risk and justified given observed hung state. It added a persistent apt config file forcing IPv4 (cmd-5729c8b7388c41f1, /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99force-ipv4) to work around IPv6 connectivity failures reaching Ubuntu mirrors — a retained system-wide config change; reasonable diagnostic-driven fix for a real connectivity problem, low-risk, but left in place without cleanup and only applied to node1, creating inconsistency with the other three nodes. Several log files (/tmp/aptupdate.log, install.log, etc.) were left behind on all four nodes as a byproduct of backgrounding apt commands — minor, low-risk residue in /tmp, not cleaned up. No destructive actions, no failed services, no security weakening, and package state is not obviously damaged. Given the session never completed its core task, most mutations reflect genuine blocked-by-infrastructure troubleshooting rather than scope creep.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-635afe86167f4ad3`, `cmd-395cf1387cde42b8`, `cmd-2c6501f4a3e241de`, `cmd-5729c8b7388c41f1`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node4:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The executor's own final report contains no selected evidence and an empty actions_performed list, so all findings here rely solely on the raw command timeline.
- The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot identity, recovered state) was not exercised at all — boot IDs are identical between before_prepare and after_executor snapshots for every node, indicating no restart was performed. This is expected given the session never reached a state where restart testing would be meaningful, but it means no restart/recovery evidence exists.
- The trace ends mid-installation; it is unknown whether a subsequent attempt (outside this captured window) would have succeeded once network connectivity to the Ubuntu mirrors stabilized.
- Command outputs are truncated/bounded per node in places, so the very last state of the apt-get install on node2 and node3 in this window is inferred from the closest available check rather than a final confirmation.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.550); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
